citations.claim: Inbound velocity just before floor impact, high speed downward
Outbound velocity after bounce exceeds inbound magnitude, despite e=0.907
First violating step: energy 3363 exceeds allowed 3324.78 (E0 3017.99)

counterfactual.change: Changed bodies[0].e from 0.9069818024722922 to 0.5 - reduces restitution to remove super-elastic bounce; same dt, steps, mass, gravity. Passing proves high e collision handling caused energy gain.

explanation: Single-body drop onto floor boundary violates energy conservation. At step 60 body is inbound vy=-18.67 with total energy ~3017 J (near E0=3017.99). Collision handling at step 61 produces outbound vy=+19.73, energy 3363 J > allowed 3324.78. Expected e=0.907 should reduce speed to ~16.9 m/s, but speed increased to 19.73, indicating impulse or positional correction adds energy instead of dissipating. Lowering e to 0.5 removes violation.
vision_note: A single blue circle drops vertically toward the bottom arena boundary across steps 58-60 and contacts the floor at step 61. At impact it does not settle or rebound with reduced speed; instead it remains at the floor with an upward velocity larger than inbound, which matches an energy-gaining bounce.
